ops.text: A smaller penalty of the same kind is reported for the FPGA decoder Sandpiper [⟦new.A5⟧], which grows weighted clusters in a sliding window, matches the defects of each neutral cluster exactly and commits one round per cycle; its circuit-level threshold of $0.672\%$ lies slightly below that of sliding-window matching on the same circuits.
Streaming FPGA designs that already commit corrections round by round, such as Sandpiper [⟦new.A5⟧], offer a natural platform for such a test.

new_bib.text: T. Ashworth, H. Pryce, K. Doyle, A. Rao, and C. Holroyd (2026). Sandpiper: sliding-window cluster matching for real-time surface-code decoding on FPGAs. arXiv.
